title: Luck and trying many ideas
summary: Streaks by luck, and why the best of many tries looks better than it is.

steps.head: Luck is everywhere
steps.body: Flip a coin 100 times. You will often see a run of 6 or 7 heads in a row. A {{streak|streak}} can come from luck alone.
steps.more: Press the button to flip again. Look at the longest run each time.

steps.head: Streaks fool the eye
steps.body: A run of wins feels like skill. Before you trust it, ask how often chance alone makes a run like that.

steps.head: Trying many ideas
steps.body: Try 50 random rules on the same past prices, and one of them will look good. The best of many tries is partly {{luck|luck}}. Then look at the same rule on new prices.

steps.head: Counting ideas tried
steps.body: This is why the Lab counts every {{idea-tried|idea tried}}. The more ideas you try, the less you should trust the best one.

steps.head: Fitting the past
steps.body: {{overfitting|Overfitting}} means a rule fits the past by chance. On new prices it then does worse.

questions.prompt: You try 50 random rules on past prices. What should you expect from the best one?

options.text: It looks good partly by luck.
options.why: Right. With so many tries, one is likely to look good even if it is random.

options.text: It will keep doing well on new prices.
options.why: No. A lucky result on old prices does not have to repeat on new ones.
No. Random rules differ, so the best of them stands out by chance.

questions.prompt: Why does the Lab count the ideas you tried?

options.text: More tries make a lucky result more likely.
options.why: Yes. The count tells you how much luck could be hiding in the best result.

options.text: To limit how much you can learn.
options.why: No. The count is there to help you judge your results, not to stop you.

options.text: To score you against other people.
options.why: No. Nothing here is a contest. The count is only for your own judgement.

questions.prompt: In 100 coin flips you see 7 heads in a row. Is the coin special?

options.text: No. Runs like that are normal.
options.why: Right. Runs of 6 or 7 are common in 100 flips of a fair coin.

options.text: Yes. A fair coin never does that.
options.why: No. A fair coin often does this in 100 flips.

options.text: Yes. The next flip must be tails.
options.why: No. Each flip is new. The coin has no memory.
